triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '19. Wider V tiling and pair-V reuse hit the register cliff' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 19. Wider V tiling and pair-V reuse hit the register cliff

problem.statement: GDN Chunk Forward Pitfalls (CuTeDSL, SM120) -- 19. Wider V tiling and pair-V reuse hit the register cliff

payload.attempted: Increase `BV` or have one CTA handle two V tiles to reuse K/Q/M/GQK work. The arithmetic work per K/Q load looks better on paper.
payload.lesson: On this shape, `BV=16` is the stable point. Attack dataflow and scratch materialization before widening V.

established_fact.mechanism: The fused K1 already carries state fragments, MMA accumulators, and multiple shared iterators. Doubling V-side state or output fragments increases long-lived registers faster than it saves K/Q staging work.

payload.observed: BV32 and pair-V probes regressed. Pair-V reduced some repeated work but pushed registers near 198 per thread and halved occupancy; BV32 similarly increased register pressure.
payload.root_cause: The fused K1 already carries state fragments, MMA accumulators, and multiple shared iterators. Doubling V-side state or output fragments increases long-lived registers faster than it saves K/Q staging work.
